entities.summary: Belarus, officially the Republic of Belarus, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe. It is bordered by Russia to the east and northeast, Ukraine to the south, Poland to the west, and Lithuania and Latvia to the northwest. The country has a hemiboreal climate and is administratively divided into six regions. Minsk is the capital and largest city; it is administered separately as a city with special status. Belarus has an area of 207,600 square kilometres (80,200 sq mi) with a population of 9.1 million. The country has a complex history, having been part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, the Russian Empire, and the Soviet Union, before gaining independence in 1991. Belarus has been influenced by various cultures and has a rich cultural heritage. The country has a significant agricultural sector and mining industry. Since its independence, Belarus has maintained close ties with Russia and has been a key player in regional politics. Belarus has also faced challenges in its democratic development and human rights record. The country has a diverse geography, with forests, lakes, and rivers making up a significant portion of its territory. Belarus has a rich cultural and historical past, with numerous historical sites and landmarks. The country has a unique blend of Eastern European and Russian influences, with a strong emphasis on tradition and community.
